raw_response:
I would start by evaluating **Mifos X**, then compare **OpenCBS Desktop**. **Cyclos 3** is a more qualified option for member payments and accounts. All three have relevant open-source editions, but I did not establish a complete, ready-to-run fit for your particular credit union.

I have treated open source, payments, banking and ledger functionality as requirements. Your question does not identify a country, operating system, payment network or accounting method, so I have not assumed any of those. The 400–1,000 members describe the intended deployment; I have not verified a capacity benchmark.

### 1. Mifos X — the first system I would evaluate

The project's [May 2013 release announcement](https://payments.mifos.org/blog/cosm-ships-mifos-x-platform-1-0/) describes an open-source financial-services platform already used by small microfinance institutions. It includes lending and integrated accounting, including journal entries outside the loan portfolio. A [July 2013 project article](https://mifos.org/blog/mlite-first-community-built-app-mifos-x-platform/) identifies the underlying core as MPL 2.0 and describes savings and accounting functionality.

That makes Mifos X a credible starting point for the operating core of a small credit union. Be precise about which application you evaluate: the same article describes **mLite as proprietary**, and its M-Pesa connection is outside the open-source core. A demonstration of that application does not establish that the complete payment integration is included in Mifos X.

The remaining question is your actual payment workflow: does the selected release handle it and post it correctly to the accounts and ledger? The [Mifos X 1.25 announcement](https://mifos.org/blog/announcing-mifos-x-1-25/) supplies more repayment/accounting detail, but it is dated **27 October 2014**, after your 15 September 2014 question. I would not backdate those added features. The July article also shows a later modification timestamp, so it is not a verified snapshot of the original page.

**Assessment:** retain as the strongest candidate to evaluate; the exact payment configuration and historical release coverage still need verification.

### 2. OpenCBS Desktop — compare the open core carefully

The [official Desktop source repository](https://github.com/OpenCBS/OpenCBS-Desktop) describes an open-source core-banking application with client, loan and savings management and a development period of 2013–2017.

The [version 14.11 user guide](https://www.opencbs.com/uploads/User%20guide%20OpenCBS%2014.11.pdf) documents repayment entry, savings interest, deposits, withdrawals and transfers. It also describes accounting rules in the free core while distinguishing separately sold modules and a configured accounting engine. The unresolved point is whether that open core provides the ledger postings and reports your institution needs. A paid-module mention alone does not prove that it fails your requirement.

Evaluate **Desktop/free core** explicitly: the current Cloud feature matrix describes a different product and cannot settle what the older Desktop edition includes. I could not establish the manual's exact publication date.

**Assessment:** retain as a plausible alternative, conditional on confirming the ledger scope of the open-source configuration.

### 3. Cyclos 3 — relevant functions, substantial version caveats

The developer explicitly identifies [Cyclos 3](https://www.cyclos.org/products/cyclos3/) as open-source banking software. Its [feature list](https://www.cyclos.org/products/cyclos3/features/) covers member accounts, loans, direct and scheduled payments, account balances, transaction histories and configurable transaction/account structures.

Those features make it relevant, but transaction histories do not by themselves establish every ledger function your credit union may mean. That part needs a concrete comparison with your accounting workflow.

The developer's current page also says **Cyclos 3 is no longer maintained and advises against mission-critical use**. That warning materially lowers its practical suitability today. I have not turned maintenance into a requirement you did not state, and I have not inferred that a later Cyclos edition has the same open-source terms.

**Assessment:** retain as a qualified candidate for comparison, with ledger coverage unverified and the maintenance warning clearly attached.

For a useful evaluation, take a representative member through account opening, a deposit, a loan disbursement, a repayment and a period-end ledger report in each selected edition. That is a proposed acceptance check, not a claim that I ran these systems. The sources establish relevant capabilities; they do not establish your complete deployment.
